sentences.text: Wodnika was a shark-like fish that measured about 1 meter (3.2 feet) in length. Unlike most of its relatives, fossils of this animal often preserve the internal cartilage skeleton, a rare feature for its kind.
Finding the internal cartilage skeleton is a surprising discovery for a fish that usually has a bony structure.
The specific shape of its tail suggests it was likely a good swimmer.
The genus Wodnika was first described by Münster in 1843.
This animal belongs to the class Chondrichthyes and the parent group Ctenacanthoidea. The genus also has the synonym Radamas.
Three species are included in the genus: Wodnika althausi, Wodnika ocoyae, and Wodnika striatula.
Wodnika lived during the Late Permian period in what is now Germany and Russia. Its time range is listed as the Wordian to Burdigalian, spanning from 266.9 to 15.98 million years ago.
